title: How Sparse Must an SAE Be to Preserve Safety-Relevant Behavioral Distinctions?
original_idea: Train SAEs at five sparsity levels on GPT-2 Small. Replace activations with SAE-reconstructed activations and measure perplexity degradation, refusal rate change, and toxic/non-toxic classification accuracy. Plot against sparsity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly practical: provides the empirical curve needed for choosing SAE sparsity in safety monitoring. Actionable result.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training five SAEs is manageable with SAELens. Measuring perplexity and classification accuracy is standard. But measuring refusal rate on GPT-2 Small (non-RLHF) is problematic.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clean ablation study structure: one variable (L1 coefficient), three metrics. Well-defined deliverable is a Pareto curve. Slightly broad with three metrics.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
